title: The Brontë Sisters
objective: After this level you can explain how Charlotte and Emily Brontë brought passionate inner voices to the novel, and why they first published as men.
summary: Charlotte, Emily and Anne Brontë published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell to avoid reviewers' treatment of women. Jane Eyre speaks in a fierce first person; Wuthering Heights storms across the moors.

cards.headline: Three new poets: Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell. None of them existed.
cards.body: Their book, Poems, came out in 1846. Behind the names were three sisters: Charlotte, Emily and Anne Brontë.

cards.headline: Why men's names?
cards.body: The sisters wanted secrecy, and they wanted to dodge the special treatment they believed reviewers gave women. Charlotte kept the name Currer Bell for her novels. Her Jane Eyre came out on October 16, 1847, and was an immediate success, far greater than the books her sisters published that same year.

cards.headline: A voice from the inside
cards.body: Jane Eyre is told in the first person by Jane herself, an orphan who becomes a governess and falls in love with her employer, Mr. Rochester. She is a thinking, feeling woman, craving love but able to give it up on principle. When Rochester tries to hold her back, she answers: "I am no bird; and no net ensnares me; I am a free human being with an independent will."

cards.headline: Passion on the moors
cards.body: Emily, as Ellis Bell, published Wuthering Heights in 1847: a highly imaginative novel of passion and hate, set on the Yorkshire moors. Early critics found it too savage, too animal-like and clumsy in construction. Two sisters, two inner storms: one speaks straight to you, the other howls across the heather.
